tenet: Use state machines / typestate — encode a multi-state protocol so illegal operations don't compile
why_discriminating: A three-state protocol (Closed -> Listening -> Established) is harder to fully type-encode than a two-state builder. The naive solution is a runtime state enum where every operation is always callable; the skillful solution puts the state in a phantom type parameter so `send` only exists on an established connection. This is the 'hard' task expected to leave headroom for a body-optimizer.
prompt: Model a network connection in Scala 3. A connection starts closed; a closed connection can be told to `listen`; a listening connection can `accept` to become established; an established connection can `send` data. Provide `Conn.closed()` returning a fresh closed connection, plus the operations `listen()`, `accept()`, and `send(data: String)` — each taking no arguments other than those shown. Output top-level definitions only — no `@main`, no tests.
